title: Can a Vision-Language Model Tune Clustering In Context?
abstract: arXiv:2611.18768v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clustering is a widely used unsupervised learning method, but selecting an appropriate algorithm and set of hyperparameters for a specific dataset can require many possible configurations and evaluations. In this work, we investigate whether a Vision-Language Model can instead visually evaluate clustering results and use those decisions to then tune an explicit clustering algorithm. We study this through three progressive experiments using Qwen3.5-27B and five controlled synthetic clustering scenarios. First, we test whether the VLM can distinguish the best clustering result from a pair of plots. Second, we test whether it can assign numerical scores to those plots where a higher score represents a better result. Finally, we use these judgments within an agentic loop in which the VLM scores a k-means clustering and proposes updated hyperparameters that may result in better clustering.
